html:
Gojoseon, "Old Joseon", was the earliest Korean state, centred in northwestern Korea and southern Manchuria. The "Go", meaning old, separates it from the Joseon dynasty founded in 1392. It was conquered by Han China in 108 BCE.

Korean tradition says it was founded in 2333 BCE by Dangun, son of a heavenly prince and a bear who became a woman. That legend first appears in a 13th-century book and is not history, but it is central to Korean identity. Both Koreas celebrate National Foundation Day on 3 October.

What the evidence shows:

  • Chinese texts name Joseon as a land beyond the state of Yan in the northeast; the earliest mentions may go back to the 7th century BCE.
  • Firm evidence dates from the 4th century BCE, when its rulers used the title of king.
  • It belonged to a Bronze Age culture known for a distinctive lute-shaped bronze dagger, found in Liaodong and Korea.

Around 194 BCE a refugee from Yan named Wiman seized the throne, starting Wiman Joseon. His grandson controlled trade between the Han and the Korean south and was caught between the Han and the Xiongnu.

In 109 to 108 BCE Emperor Wu of Han invaded and took the capital, near modern Pyongyang. The Han set up the Four Commanderies, of which Lelang lasted until 313 CE. Chinese writing and goods spread through them into Korea.

After Gojoseon came the kingdoms that grew into the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
sum: Gojoseon, "Old Joseon", was the earliest Korean state, centred in northwestern Korea and southern Manchuria. The "Go", meaning old, separates it from the Joseon dynasty founded in 1392. It was conquered by Han China in 108 BCE.
